articles.title: Como o ar mais limpo acelera o aquecimento global — e vem revelando um problema maior | G1
articles.standfirst: Redução da poluição pode estar contribuindo para acelerar o aquecimento global, apontam estudos.
articles.summary: Redução da poluição pode estar contribuindo para acelerar o aquecimento global, apontam estudos.
articles.body:
Emissões de gases do efeito estufa podem provocar aquecimento maior do que o previsto, apontam novas evidências. — Foto: AFP via Getty Images

No mês de julho, o Reino Unido registrou recordes de calor. E, paralelamente, surgiu uma curiosa discussão no X, em relação à ciência climática.

O vice-líder do partido de direita radical Reform UK, Richard Tice, compartilhou uma reportagem do jornal britânico The Telegraph com o título: "As ondas de calor causadas pela queda da poluição".

Ele afirmou que o ar mais limpo, não o dióxido de carbono, seria responsável pelo aumento das temperaturas e que a população teria sido "ludibriada".

Tice estava errado ao indicar que o dióxido de carbono não seria o principal causador do aquecimento global. Mas a ciência distorcida por ele é real — e muito mais interessante que sua afirmação original.

Os combustíveis fósseis que estamos queimando há mais de um século produzem dois tipos muito diferentes de poluição.

Como sabemos, o dióxido de carbono aquece a Terra. Mas a poluição por enxofre é muito menos conhecida.

Ela forma imensas quantidades de minúsculas partículas no ar, que refletem a luz do Sol de volta para o espaço. Este processo combate, em parte, o efeito do carbono sobre o aquecimento.

As políticas de ar limpo adotadas em todo o mundo (como o programa de combate à chuva ácida dos Estados Unidos, no início dos anos 1990) reduziram a poluição causada pelos gases das usinas de energia. Com isso, as emissões de enxofre vêm apresentando forte queda, enquanto o dióxido de carbono se mantém próximo dos recordes de alta.

Os cientistas acreditam cada vez mais que a perda desse efeito resfriador cause leve aceleração do aquecimento global.

Gráfico dos anos mais quentes. — Foto: BBC

Os três últimos anos foram os mais quentes já registrados. E o Serviço Meteorológico do Reino Unido afirma que 2027, "muito provavelmente", irá ultrapassar 2024 como o ano mais quente da história.

Longe das redes sociais, a discussão sobre o tweet de Tice levantou uma questão ainda mais interessante — e preocupante. Seria possível que o nosso planeta seja realmente mais sensível aos gases do efeito estufa do que imaginávamos?

E, se for verdade, o clima poderá estar mudando com mais rapidez do que temíamos?

As temperaturas globais variam naturalmente entre um ano e outro. O El Niño, por exemplo, um fenômeno natural que ocorre no oceano Pacífico, pode aumentar temporariamente o calor no planeta.

Por isso, uma série de anos com recorde de calor não significa, necessariamente, que a velocidade do aquecimento global tenha aumentado.

Reto Knutti e sua equipe do Instituto Federal de Tecnologia (ETH, na sigla em alemão) de Zurique, na Suíça, tentaram extrair os efeitos do El Niño e de outras flutuações naturais para revelar a a tendência real oculta pelos números.

"Fica muito claro que a velocidade do aquecimento aumentou", afirma Knutti. Ele é professor de física climática na universidade suíça e foi autor coordenador do Painel Intergovernamental sobre Mudanças Climáticas (IPCC, na sigla em inglês), o organismo mantido pela ONU que produz as avaliações mais respeitadas sobre ciência climática do mundo.

Outro estudo, publicado neste ano, chegou a uma conclusão similar ao considerar diversas influências naturais importantes. E, aparentemente, os aerossóis fazem parte da equação.

A queima de petróleo e carvão libera dióxido de enxofre, que forma minúsculas partidas conhecidas como aerossóis de sulfato. Estas partículas são brilhantes e refletem parte da luz solar, antes que ela atinja e aqueça a superfície do planeta.

A poluição dos navios pode criar rastros brilhantes através das nuvens, que são visíveis do espaço — Foto: Nasa

Você provavelmente já ouviu a analogia da estufa, empregada para explicar o aquecimento global. Gases como dióxido de carbono dificultam a fuga do calor da Terra, como as janelas de vidro de uma estufa.

Muito bem. A poluição causada pelo enxofre age mais ou menos como a poeira sobre essas janelas. Quanto mais poeira se acumular, menos luz do Sol irá entrar e a estufa irá se aquecer mais lentamente.

Øivind Hodnebrog é um dos principais pesquisadores do instituto de pesquisa climática Cicero, na Noruega. Ele estuda como a queda da poluição dos aerossóis afeta o clima do planeta.

"Os aerossóis de sulfato são partículas muito pequenas, mas brilhantes", explica ele. E, além de refletirem a luz solar, os aerossóis também resfriam o planeta alterando a formação das nuvens.

Os aerossóis agem como sementes minúsculas, em torno das quais o vapor d'água pode se condensar. Com isso, algumas nuvens ficam mais brilhantes ou têm vida mais longa.

A poluição dos navios pode até criar rastros brilhantes nas nuvens sobre o oceano, que são visíveis do espaço. Por isso, o aumento dos aerossóis pode significar nuvens mais brilhantes, maior reflexão e, com isso, redução do aquecimento.

A poluição causada pelo enxofre contribuiu para a chuva ácida que destruiu florestas como em 1990, no território da antiga Checoslováquia — Foto: Corbis Via Getty Images

Mas a poluição por enxofre também prejudica a saúde humana. Ela pode entrar nos nossos pulmões, dificultando a respiração.

Ela também causa a chuva ácida, que pode destruir as florestas e matar os peixes. Por isso, alguns países passaram décadas tentando reduzi-la.

As emissões caíram sensivelmente na Europa, América do Norte e na China. Paralelamente, novas regras também reduziram a poluição por enxofre do setor de navegação.

Na nossa analogia da estufa, é como se tivéssemos limpado parte da poeira das janelas, aumentando a incidência da luz solar.

O dióxido de carbono permanece no sistema climático por séculos, mas os aerossóis de sulfato sobrevivem na atmosfera por alguns dias ou semanas. Por isso, quando as emissões de enxofre são reduzidas, seu efeito de resfriamento desaparece quase instantaneamente.

O efeito é mais forte quando a poluição causada pelo enxofre cai com maior rapidez. Um estudo estima que o enxofre aumentou o aquecimento do verão no centro-oeste da Europa em cerca de meio grau desde 1980.

O professor e cientista climático Piers Forster, da Universidade de Leeds, no Reino Unido, outro autor da avaliação mais recente do IPCC, calcula que a redução da poluição de aerossóis pode, agora, acrescentar cerca de 0,05 °C a 0,1 °C de aquecimento por década.

Mas os aerossóis só explicam parte da recente aceleração do aquecimento. Os gases do efeito estufa permanecem sendo muito mais importantes.

Forster calcula que os gases acrescentem atualmente cerca de 0,2 °C ao aquecimento global por década.

A redução dos aerossóis é "muito significativa", declarou ele. "Mas é muito menos importante que a contribuição dos gases do efeito estufa."

"Os aerossóis mascararam parte do aquecimento causado pelos gases do efeito estufa desde o princípio", explica Hodnebrog.

"Mascararam." Esta é uma palavra interessante.

O que ele quer dizer é que o ar mais limpo não está causando o aquecimento, mas sim retirando parte do resfriamento que, antes, retardava o aumento do calor.

Mas, se o ar mais limpo é responsável por apenas uma parte da recente aceleração do aquecimento global, o que mais estará acontecendo?

Enfraquecimento das nuvens e aquecimento dos oceanos

Para observar o que mais pode estar ocorrendo, os cientistas se afastam e analisam o planeta como um todo: quanta energia a Terra absorve do Sol e quanto calor ela perde no espaço.

Os cientistas chamam a diferença de desequilíbrio energético da Terra.

O ar mais limpo faz parte deste quadro. Menos partículas de sulfato significam menor reflexão da luz solar. Na nossa analogia da estufa, as janelas estão mais limpas.

Por muito tempo, a Terra vem absorvendo mais energia do que perde. Este excedente é o que aquece o planeta.

Knutti explica que este desequilíbrio praticamente triplicou ao longo das últimas duas décadas, mas o aumento preciso depende de quais anos forem comparados.

Os gases do efeito estufa funcionam principalmente dificultando o escape do calor para o espaço. Todos nós sabemos disso.

Mas, quando observamos o desequilíbrio energético da Terra, percebemos que também existe mais luz do Sol entrando e, portanto, mais calor que pode ser absorvido.

O que mais pode estar permitindo o aumento da entrada de luz solar?

O ex-presidente americano George H. W. Bush (1924-2018) assinou a histórica iniciativa do ar limpo em 1991, com o então primeiro-ministro canadense, Brian Mulroney (1939-2024). Seu objetivo era reduzir a chuva ácida. — Foto: Getty Images

Grande parte desta mudança aparentemente envolve um ponto já mencionado nesta reportagem: as nuvens.

Observamos como a poluição causada pelo enxofre pode fazer algumas nuvens ficarem mais brilhantes e terem vida mais longa, refletindo mais a luz do Sol. Mas o próprio aquecimento global também pode alterar as nuvens.

À medida que algumas regiões do oceano se aquecem, a cobertura de nuvens baixas pode diminuir.

Isso faz diferença porque as nuvens são brilhantes e o oceano embaixo delas é escuro. Com menos nuvens, a luz do Sol sobre o mar aumenta e grande parte dela é absorvida na forma de calor.

Este processo se retroalimenta. O aquecimento reduz a cobertura de nuvens, o que permite o aumento da entrada de luz solar, que produz ainda mais aquecimento. E os oceanos certamente estão se aquecendo.

Segundo a Organização Meteorológica Mundial, os oceanos se aqueceram com rapidez mais de duas vezes maior ao longo das últimas duas décadas, em comparação com o período entre 1960 e 2005.

O físico climático Paulo Ceppi, do Imperial College de Londres, afirma que, segundo suas pesquisas, este ciclo de retroalimentação entre as mudanças climáticas e as nuvens é mais importante que a poluição por enxofre para explicar o recente declínio da cobertura de nuvens em baixa altitude.

Mas ainda existem muitas incertezas. Os cientistas afirmam que os impactos do ar mais limpo, as variações naturais e os efeitos do próprio aquecimento estão todos relacionados entre si.

Perguntei a Reto Knutti qual a participação de cada um desses fatores na mudança da cobertura de nuvens. Ele respondeu simplesmente: "Não sabemos."

É aqui que a história toma um rumo ainda mais preocupante.

Esta incerteza é relevante porque as nuvens são um dos fatores mais difíceis de serem representados nas simulações computadorizadas empregadas pelos cientistas para projetar o aquecimento futuro. Alguns modelos mostram mais aquecimento do que outros, com a mesma quantidade de emissão de gases do efeito estufa.

Os cientistas chamam esta variabilidade de "sensibilidade climática", ou seja, a magnitude da reação do clima a gases como o dióxido de carbono. E as observações recentes oferecem a Knutti e seus colegas uma nova forma de testar estes modelos.

Eles descobriram que os modelos que apresentaram as melhores previsões do recente aquecimento, além do maior desequilíbrio energético da Terra, são também os que demonstram um clima mais sensível.

Em outras palavras, os modelos que preveem maior aquecimento aparentemente são os mais precisos.

A análise da sua equipe indica que o mesmo volume de emissões poderá produzir cerca de 25% mais aquecimento do que pensávamos anteriormente.

Cientistas afirmam que, se o aquecimento global se acelerar, devemos esperar mais incêndios florestais, como os que ocorreram no ano passado em Los Angeles, nos Estados Unidos — Foto: AFP via Getty Images

Um estudo publicado no ano passado pela revista Science indica uma direção similar. Os modelos que projetaram aquecimento relativamente baixo tiveram mais dificuldade para reproduzir o aumento observado no desequilíbrio energético da Terra.

Com as políticas governamentais atualmente em vigor, calcula-se que o mundo caminhe para atingir cerca de 2,8 °C de aquecimento até o final do século. Mas Piers Forster afirma que, se as novas evidências se mostrarem corretas, o mesmo rumo geral das emissões poderá atingir aquecimento mais próximo de 3,5 °C.

Parece algo sério, mas existem razões importantes para mantermos cautela.

O aquecimento parece estar mais rápido, mas Forster explica que isso não significa que ele continuará se acelerando. Ele indica que as recentes observações que sustentam estas estimativas cobrem um período relativamente curto.

"Precisamos ter muito cuidado em relação ao caminho a tomar para interpretar observações que cobrem uma ou duas décadas", segundo ele.

O registro de satélites é curto, as variações naturais são grandes e os novos estudos não eliminam as estimativas anteriores. Mas, ainda assim, existem cientistas alarmados com a situação.

A limpeza do ar está agravando o aquecimento global?

Estritamente falando, sim. A retirada da poluição por sulfato elimina parte do resfriamento que vinha compensando o efeito estufa. Este fator realmente contribuiu para a recente aceleração, mas o ar mais limpo não causa mudanças climáticas.

A questão dos aerossóis pode ajudar a explicar parte desta aceleração. Mas as evidências mais amplas levantam uma possibilidade mais preocupante: que a reação do clima aos gases do efeito estufa é mais forte do que consideravam as principais estimativas.

Se isso for correto, as mesmas emissões poderão produzir mais aquecimento que o esperado.

Os riscos climáticos crescem a cada fração de grau de aquecimento. E o aumento das temperaturas pode causar ondas de calor mais fortes, cheias, secas e incêndios florestais.

Parte da ciência detalhada nesta reportagem é complexa e questões importantes ainda aguardam resolução.

Mas a ciência é clara sobre a questão fundamental: quanto mais gases do efeito estufa emitirmos, mais quente ficará o planeta.

E, se o clima da Terra, de fato, for mais sensível do que pensávamos, reduzir rapidamente as emissões passa a ser uma questão ainda mais importante.

articles.title: Mega-Sena acumula em R$ 95 milhões; Lavras e Varginha têm ganhadores | G1
articles.standfirst: Concurso 3.057 não teve ganhador das seis dezenas. No Sul de Minas, uma aposta de Lavras acertou a quina e faturou mais de R$ 31 mil.
articles.summary: A Mega-Sena acumulou em R$ 95 milhões após o concurso 3.057, que premiou uma aposta de Lavras com a quina e quatro moradores de Varginha na quadra.
articles.body:
Quatro apostas feitas em Varginha acertaram quatro dezenas no concurso 3.057 da Mega-Sena, sorteado neste domingo (13), em São Paulo. Cada uma delas vai receber R$ 863,24.

Ninguém acertou as seis dezenas sorteadas (02-04-16-21-48-53 ), e o prêmio principal acumulou para R$ 95 milhões.

No Sul de Minas, o principal destaque foi uma aposta de bolão registrada em Lavras, na lotérica Lotomania Loterias, que acertou cinco números e faturou R$ 31.872,72. O bolão tinha oito cotas.

Mega-Sena, concurso 3057 — Foto: Reprodução

Em Varginha, as apostas premiadas na quadra foram registradas nas lotéricas Lotérica Nossa S de Fátima, Trevo da Sorte e Varginha Centenário loterias Ltda, além de outra aposta feita na cidade. Todas receberam prêmio de R$ 863,24.

Outras cidades da região também tiveram apostas contempladas na faixa de quatro acertos, entre elas Alfenas, Areado, Baependi, Boa Esperança, Cambuí, Caxambu, Extrema, Itajubá, Machado, Muzambinho, Poços de Caldas, Pouso Alegre, Santa Rita do Sapucaí, São Lourenço e Três Pontas.

Segundo a Caixa, 86 apostas em todo o país acertaram a quina e levaram R$ 31.872,72 cada. Já a quadra teve 5.234 apostas ganhadoras, com prêmio individual de R$ 863,24.

articles.summary: Trecho tinha sido interditado às 2h da madrugada do último sábado (12) por causa do alto volume de chuva.
articles.body:
A Serra Antiga da rodovia dos Tamoios foi liberada por volta das 15h deste domingo (13) após 37 horas de interdição. A pista havia sido interditada às 2h da madrugada do último sábado (12) por causa do alto volume de chuva, que pode provocar queda de barreiras.

Serra Antiga da Tamoios é liberada — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Durante o período de interdição, o fluxo na rodovia foi em operação comboio pela Serra Nova, com sistema pare e siga, alternando os trajetos. Foram realizados 34 comboios.

No fim da manhã deste domingo, uma carreta quebrou em um dos túneis da Serra Nova, o que paralisou o trânsito por completo. O tráfego voltou ao sistema de comboio por volta das 13h40.

articles.summary: O concurso Valença para professores oferece 96 vagas de níveis médio e superior com inscrições até 5 de outubro e provas previstas para novembro.
articles.body:
A prefeitura de Valença (RJ) abriu inscrições para o concurso de contratação de professores da rede municipal de ensino. Ao todo, serão oferecidas 96 vagas imediatas, além da formação de cadastro de reserva.

Os interessados devem se inscrever no site até o dia 5 de outubro (segunda-feira). O valor da taxa de inscrição é de R$ 66 para nível médio e R$ 68 para nível superior .

Segundo a prefeitura, das oportunidades, 70 são para professor III, cargo onde é necessário ter fomação de nível médio na modalidade normal/formação de professores ou licenciatura em pedagogia.

Ainda de acordo com a administração municipal, as demais vagas são para professor IV, com exigência de formação superior na área correspondente (confira abaixo).

A prefeitura informou também que a seleção apresenta uma estrutura de avaliação com prova objetiva, análise de títulos e pontuação vinculada à prova nacional docente. A prova objetiva está marcada para o dia 22 de novembro e vai contar com 50 questões, sendo 10 de conhecimentos básicos, 10 complementares e 30 de específicos (com peso 2).

Os candidatos aprovados serão convocados para a avaliação de títulos. A etapa valerá até oito pontos e poderá considerar doutorado, mestrado, especialização lato sensu, graduação adicional e a nota da prova nacional docente.

articles.title: Justiça barra retomada de área da Abor pela Prefeitura de Santos | G1
articles.standfirst: No local, a Associação Beneficente Osvaldo De Rosis (Abor) oferece atividades esportivas à população há mais de 25 anos. Administração municipal pretendia utilizar o terreno para construir uma Vila Criativa e ampliar a policlínica.
articles.summary: Justiça extingue ação da Prefeitura de Santos contra a Associação Osvaldo De Rosis, garantindo a permanência das atividades esportivas na Ponta da Praia após falhas no processo administrativo.
articles.body:
Área de 5 mil metros quadrados é ocupada pela Associação Beneficente Osvaldo De Rosis (Abor) — Foto: Alexsander Ferraz/A Tribuna Jornal

Uma decisão da 2ª Vara da Fazenda Pública de Santos, no litoral de São Paulo, extinguiu um processo movido pela Prefeitura de Santos para retomar uma área de 5 mil metros quadrados cedida à Associação Beneficente Osvaldo De Rosis (Abor), na Ponta da Praia. A prefeitura ainda pode recorrer da decisão.

No local, situado na Praça Primeiro de Maio, a entidade oferece atividades esportivas à população há mais de 25 anos. A administração municipal pretendia utilizar o terreno para construir uma Vila Criativa e ampliar a policlínica do bairro.

Na decisão, datada de 27 de agosto, o juiz André Luís Maciel Carneiro entendeu que o município não cumpriu etapas formais necessárias antes de recorrer à Justiça.

Como a entidade ocupava o espaço com base em um Termo de Permissão e Uso válido até 2028, a prefeitura deveria ter feito uma notificação formal e prévia, concedendo prazo razoável para a desocupação. Segundo o magistrado, isso não ocorreu, já que a Administração utilizou apenas e-mails informais para comunicar a associação.

O juiz reforçou a necessidade de uma "notificação prévia, regular e inequívoca, com a fixação de prazo razoável para a desocupação". Na decisão, concluiu que "correspondências eletrônicas informais desprovidas de formalidade legal e sem a concessão de prazo idôneo para restituição do bem público não suprem a exigência formal de notificação".

A prefeitura também alegou que a associação teria cometido desvio de finalidade ao utilizar o espaço público para atividades que estariam fora do escopo original da cessão. O magistrado, porém, apontou que uma acusação desse tipo exige a abertura de um processo administrativo prévio, garantindo à entidade o direito à ampla defesa e ao contraditório antes de uma eventual ação judicial para retomada da área.

Com a extinção do processo, o município foi condenado ao pagamento das despesas processuais e dos honorários advocatícios. Em nota, a Prefeitura de Santos informou apenas que adotará as providências cabíveis dentro do prazo legal.

O advogado que representa a associação, Caio Machado Nunes, criticou a postura da administração em nota enviada à imprensa. Segundo ele, representantes da entidade procuraram a prefeitura e aceitaram ceder parte da área para permitir a execução dos projetos pretendidos pelo município.

“A resposta foi categórica: ou entregávamos toda a área, ou não haveria acordo. Diante disso, fica difícil enxergar essa postura como uma simples necessidade administrativa. Na prática, queriam inviabilizar a continuidade do Instituto. Esperamos que, agora, diante da decisão da Justiça, a Prefeitura reveja essa medida absurda”, afirmou o advogado.

O defensor também ressaltou que a decisão ainda não transitou em julgado. “O caso segue em andamento, com prazos e instâncias à disposição das partes. Nossos advogados acompanham cada etapa e adotarão todas as medidas cabíveis para defender nossos alunos e os interesses da comunidade”, finalizou.

Procurado, o vereador Rui de Rosis Jr. (PL), neto do político que dá nome ao instituto, comemorou a decisão e alegou perseguição política.

"A decisão da Justiça confirma o que denunciamos desde o início: para tentar parar minhas denúncias sobre gastos absurdos e injustificáveis, a Prefeitura atropelou o devido processo legal e atacou uma instituição que atende a população de Santos há mais de vinte anos", disse.

articles.title: Homem desaparecido após ser arrastado por correnteza é encontrado morto em Jandira | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, três pessoas foram arrastadas pela força da água na madrugada de sábado (12); uma mulher conseguiu se salvar e o segundo homem segue desaparecido.
articles.summary: Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, três pessoas foram arrastadas pela força da água na madrugada de sábado (12); uma mulher conseguiu se salvar e o segundo homem segue desaparecido.
articles.body:
Um dos dois homens que desapareceram após serem arrastados pela correnteza de um rio durante uma enchente em Jandira , na Grande São Paulo, foi encontrado morto na tarde deste domingo (13). O outro homem continua desaparecido e é procurado pelas equipes de resgate.

O caso aconteceu por volta da 1h deste sábado (12), na Avenida Antônio Bardella, no bairro Jardim São Luiz.

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, uma das vítima estava em uma área atingida pela enchente quando o outro homem e a irmã dele, de 32 anos, tentaram ajudá-lo. Durante a tentativa de resgate, a força da correnteza arrastou os três.

A mulher conseguiu sair da água ao se agarrar em árvores na margem do rio. Ela foi posteriormente encaminhada para atendimento médico, mas perdeu contato com os dois homens.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado para realizar as buscas pelos desaparecidos com apoio da Defesa Civil Municipal. O caso foi registrado na Delegacia de Jandira.

Imagem ilustrativa - viatura do Corpo de Bombeiros — Foto: Claudio Vitor Vaz/Arquivo A Tribuna Jornal

A Defesa Civil do Estado acompanha as condições meteorológicas por meio de radares e satélites e mantém equipes mobilizadas para atender possíveis ocorrências.

Diante da possibilidade de novas chuvas, o órgão recomenda que a população:

fique atenta a sinais de risco em encostas e áreas próximas a córregos;

procure um local seguro durante temporais;

acompanhe os boletins e alertas oficiais da Defesa Civil.

A população pode receber gratuitamente alertas no celular por meio do serviço de SMS da Defesa Civil. Para se cadastrar, basta enviar o CEP da localidade para o número 40199.

Em caso de emergência, os telefones são 193, do Corpo de Bombeiros, e 199, da Defesa Civil.

O candidato do PSD participou, às 9h de reuniões e visitas na Aldeia Kumenê, Oiapoque . Às 13h, o candidato seguiu teve compromissos e encontro com lideranças e moradores na Aldeia Kumarumã.

O candidato do PCO realizou, às 9h, um cômicio na praça da cidade Itaubal e às 12h seguiu para um almoço com agricultores. Às 17h realizou uma reunião com lideranças do municipío.

articles.title: Festa de Nossa Senhora das Dores em Divinópolis tem missas e procissão | G1
articles.standfirst: Dia da padroeira é celebrado na terça-feira (15) na igreja do bairro Nações. Também está prevista uma procissão pelas principais ruas do bairro.
articles.summary: A celebração de Nossa Senhora das Dores em Divinópolis conta com missas, procissão e barraquinhas no Bairro Nações nesta terça-feira (15).
articles.body:
Igreja matriz que leva o nome da padroeira está localizada na rua Argentina, n° 431, no Bairro Nações — Foto: Mariana Gonçalves/g1

O Dia de Nossa Senhora das Dores celebrado na terça-feira (15) será comemorado com missas, barraquinhas e procissão em Divinópolis . A igreja matriz que leva o nome da padroeira está localizada na rua Argentina, n° 431, no Bairro Nações.

Segundo a Diocese de Divinópolis, Nossa Senhora das Dores ou Mãe Dolorosa, é um dos vários títulos que a Virgem Maria recebeu ao longo da história. Este título se refere as sete dores que Nossa Senhora sofreu ao longo da vida, principalmente nos momentos da Paixão de Cristo.

7h – Celebração Eucarística presidida pelo reverendíssimo padre Welington Rodrigues. Coral: Iluminai. Convidados: Matriz e Festeiros do Dia.

18h30 – Terço de Nossa Senhora das Dores. Responsáveis: Matriz, Todas as Pastorais e Movimentos.

19h30 - Celebração Eucarística presidida pelo reverendíssimo com o padre Ailson de Oliveira Ceccotti. Convidados: Matriz, Todas as Comunidades da Paróquia e Festeiros do Dia.

As barraquinhas de comidas começam após o fim da última missa.

Às 19h será realizada a procissão com a Imagem de Nossa Senhora das Dores saindo da porta da igreja matriz e percorrendo as ruas do entorno.

A TV Mirante realiza, a partir desta segunda-feira (14) até o dia 21 de setembro, uma série de entrevistas com os candidatos ao Governo do Maranhão nas eleições de 2026.

As entrevistas serão exibidas ao vivo no JMTV 1ª Edição , com duração de 30 minutos para cada candidato. O g1 Maranhão também fará a transmissão ao vivo.

A ordem dos candidatos, assim como os dias e horários das entrevistas, foi definida por sorteio, realizado no dia 6 de setembro , na presença dos representantes das candidaturas, durante reunião no Grupo Mirante.

Veja quem são os candidatos a governador no Maranhão — Foto: Montagem g1

Os candidatos serão entrevistados pelos apresentadores Tayse Feques e Rodrigo Bonfim e responderão a perguntas elaboradas por 32 estudantes maranhenses , que representarão os eleitores durante a dinâmica.

Os estudantes ficarão posicionados atrás dos candidatos e dos apresentadores durante as entrevistas. As perguntas serão colocadas em uma urna e sorteadas ao vivo.

Além das perguntas elaboradas pelos estudantes, os candidatos também deverão responder a questionamentos enviados pelos eleitores.

A segunda edição da Rota da Cerveja Divinópolis acontece de 19 de setembro a 5 de dezembro, com oito estabelecimentos participantes. O público poderá curtir shows de artistas regionais, provar comidas típicas e conhecer mais sobre a produção local de cerveja.

A Rota contempla tanto as cervejarias com produção própria quanto as 'cervejarias ciganas' — aquelas registradas na cidade, mas que utilizam fábricas parceiras para a produção.

articles.summary: SURAT: At least 75 students of a private boarding school in Surat fell sick with suspected food poisoning, with 12 of them requiring hospitalisation, .
articles.body: SURAT: At least 75 students of a private boarding school in Surat fell sick with suspected food poisoning, with 12 of them requiring hospitalisation, an official said on Sunday.All the students are out of danger, he said.The students, who reside in the hostel of P P Savani School in Abrama area, began developing symptoms including diarrhoea and vomiting from Saturday night, said Surat Municipal Corporation Medical Health Officer P H Umrigar.Of the 12 students admitted to hospital, nine are girls and all are aged between 15 and 17 years. Four have since been discharged after treatment, while the condition of the remaining students is stable, Umrigar said.Following the incident, the SMC health department initiated action, the civic body said in a release.Teams from the Food, Health and Sanitation departments inspected the school hostel and collected four food samples, which were sent for testing, the civic body said.A mobile medical team is also conducting health check-ups of other students staying at the hostel.Around 2,200 students and 300 staff members are housed at the boarding school. articles.title: In 2021, a developer bought an empty Park City lot for $6 million; 5 years and 4 years of construction later, the 17,000-sq-ft home has sold for a city-record $37 million
articles.summary: Real Estate News: A vacant piece of mountain land in Park City, Utah, bought for $6 million in 2021, has been turned into a $37 million luxury home, setting the highest.
articles.body: A vacant piece of mountain land in Park City, Utah, bought for $6 million in 2021, has been turned into a $37 million luxury home, setting the highest residential sale price ever recorded within the city limits. The record-breaking off-market deal was first reported by The Wall Street Journal. Covering 17,000 square feet, the newly completed home was sold after four years of construction overseen by Rhode Island-based developer Raymond Uritescu, Chief Executive Officer of Providence Realty Investments. Estate broker Steve Jury of Keller Williams Park City, who represented both sides of the deal, confirmed the final $37 million sale price to The Wall Street Journal. The figure beats previous residential sales records within the official boundaries of the well-known ski resort town.Four years of construction in Deer ValleyThe property sits on a multi-acre lot inside a private, gated community in the Deer Valley resort area. When Providence Realty Investments bought the land five years ago, it was completely undeveloped. Uritescu began preparing the site and laying the groundwork soon after the $6 million purchase in 2021. Construction then continued for four years. Building a mansion of this size in the mountain environment brought major challenges. Seasonal weather, steep terrain and strict local building rules in the Deer Valley area can limit construction to the warmer months. Despite these difficulties, workers completed the nine-bedroom home, designed to meet the needs of wealthy modern buyers. Details reported by The Wall Street Journal said the property was built with large timber frames, high-performance insulated glass designed for severe winter weather and custom stonework chosen to fit with the surrounding Utah landscape. The design also uses large floor-to-ceiling windows to give residents wide views of the surrounding mountains.High-end features drive record priceThe home has extensive ski-in, ski-out facilities, giving residents direct private access to Deer Valley Resort's ski trails. Inside, it features a professional-grade chef's kitchen, custom wine storage, heated outdoor patios for year-round use and large wellness facilities. The wellness area includes a private spa, indoor swimming pool and fitness centre. The property was sold fully completed and ready for the buyer to move in. When contacted by The Wall Street Journal, Uritescu declined to discuss the project's financial margins, funding or the identity of the private buyer. Broker Steve Jury also refused to provide personal details about the buyer, citing strict non-disclosure agreements common in high-profile local property deals.Limited supply boosts Utah mountain marketThe sale shows the continued strength of the luxury housing market in Utah's leading resort communities. Some areas outside Park City's official city limits, including the Snyderville Basin and nearby private club communities, have at times recorded higher prices for large compounds or extensive land holdings. However, this deal sets a new benchmark for a single-family home located within Park City itself. Local market data cited by The Wall Street Journal shows that the supply of new, large homes inside the city remains very limited. High land prices, long permitting processes and a shortage of remaining buildable land have created a major supply gap for completed homes larger than 10,000 square feet. Because of this shortage, wealthy buyers have shown they are willing to pay large premiums for finished luxury homes. Buying a completed property also allows them to avoid the years of delays that can come with purchasing undeveloped land and managing a complicated construction project themselves. The $37 million sale completes a lucrative five-year development project for Providence Realty Investments. The company has transformed an initial $6 million land purchase into one of the most valuable single-family residential properties recently completed in Utah.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Built in 1966, San Francisco's Empress of China closed in 2016; 10 years later, a collaborative founded by six nonprofits returned it to community ownership and reopened its doors
articles.summary: US News: San Francisco's historic Empress of China building has returned to community ownership a decade after closing, following its purchase by a group forme.
articles.body: San Francisco's historic Empress of China building has returned to community ownership a decade after closing, following its purchase by a group formed by six leading Asian American non-profit organisations. The Chinatown Media and Arts Collaborative announced the purchase of the landmark six-storey property at 838 Grant Avenue, clearing the way to turn the former banquet venue into a permanent arts and cultural campus. Built in 1966, the venue was an important gathering place for generations of Chinatown families and visitors before closing its doors in 2016. The return to community ownership was marked by a public open house called "The Empress Re-Imagined", giving residents a chance to enter the historic building for the first time in 10 years. Details about the purchase and long-term plans were published by the Chinatown Media and Arts Collaborative and SF Station.Six non-profits unite for historic purchaseThe purchase was made by the Chinatown Media and Arts Collaborative, an alliance formed in 2017 by six Asian American non-profit organisations. The group includes the Angel Island Immigration Station Foundation, the Chinese Culture Foundation of San Francisco, the Chinese Historical Society of America, the Center for Asian American Media, the Chinatown Community Development Center, and Chinese for Affirmative Action. The joint initiative was created on the belief that local residents and cultural organisations should have direct control over property to protect the neighbourhood's heritage. By securing ownership of 838 Grant Avenue, the coalition hopes to prevent commercial displacement and keep the venue focused on public and community use. Funding for the purchase and the first stage of changes to the building came from philanthropic support. This included grants from the Svane Family Foundation, Grants for the Arts, the San Francisco Arts Commission, and the San Francisco Foundation.Plan for a neighbourhood arts campusUnder the plan outlined by the Chinatown Media and Arts Collaborative, the 17,000-square-foot building will undergo long-term planning to create an integrated cultural campus. The facility is expected to work alongside the collaborative's nearby location at 800 Grant Avenue, creating a connected group of arts venues along the neighbourhood's main commercial corridor. The plan calls for the building's multiple floors to be turned into public galleries, performance halls, archival exhibition areas, and artist residency studios. Instead of operating only as a traditional museum, the venue will serve as an active space where local artists, historians and civic advocates can work together on public projects.Statements published by the Chinatown Media and Arts Collaborative from Mabel Teng, co-Executive Director of the organisation, stressed the importance of local institutions having control over the property. "The Chinese name for this open house event is 皇后有請, which translates to 'The Empress is Inviting You In.' We hope people will walk through these doors, feel a deep sense of ownership, and recognize that this space is theirs to shape," says Mabel Teng, co-Executive Director, CMAC. "CMAC was founded on the conviction that Chinatown has the agency to tell and amplify its own stories, and our transformation of the iconic Empress of China is a vital step in this direction."Co-Executive Director Stephen Gong also highlighted the importance of the project, saying the physical restoration of the building is part of a wider economic and cultural recovery plan for the area. "CMAC is undergoing long-range planning to transform this landmark into a dynamic cultural campus—a place where the community and visitors can find a safe sense of belonging. This open house is a warm invitation to everyone to join the conversation. Together, we can transform Grant Avenue into a constellation of art hubs driven by community architecture, design, and creativity," says Stephen Gong, co-Executive Director, CMAC.Public open house begins a new chapterThe community open house gave visitors their first look at temporary interior installations created for the reopening. Visual artist Summer Lee redesigned the ground-floor space as a communal lounge, using furniture and display fixtures to encourage people to gather and reflect on the building's history. The reopening programme included cultural performances involving different generations. These included a traditional First Nations drumming ceremony by Mike Ballenger, Buddhist blessings by Ven. Ta Chun Shih of Miu Kuang Temple and Ven. Yanmi Shi of the Guanyin Meditation Center, along with live performances by Lion Dance ME and the Young Woman's Choral Projects. Historical film projections and displays of archival photographs were presented across the upper floors, showing the venue's history of more than 50 years as a major banquet hall. Additional community workshops were held with Richmond Area Multi-Services, Inc. and ShadowLight Productions. The sessions included interactive shadow puppetry and archival photography projects led by local artists. The Chinatown Media and Arts Collaborative is now preparing master renovation plans for the building. Details about construction dates and the different stages of architectural work will be announced after a series of public community design sessions planned for the coming months.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: China Is Worried About Russia’s Growing Ties With North Korea
articles.summary: China is wary of North Korea's closer relationship with Russia. While this partnership may cause more stress for the West, it also creates stress for Beijing...
articles.body:
Vladmir Putin knows he has a problem. The war is costing Russia about $290 billion per year. Russia is losing 30,000 troops a month. Its advance is not just stalling but also reversing in some places. And the Russian public is feeling the cost of war in more tangible ways. Ukrainian drones hit a St. Petersburg oil terminal and nearby port in July of this year. On top of that in late 2025, Russia announced that value added taxes were going up to 22% , with food prices surging up 18% in 2026 as well.

Putin is so desperate that he started to rely on troops from North Korea, one of the poorest countries in the world. South Korea's Defence Intelligence Agency estimates that North Korea has sent more than 16,000 personnel to Russia since October of 2024 and supplied it with more than 15 million artillery rounds. Pyongyang has also provided Russia with dozens of KN-23 and KN-24 missiles.

Ukraine has suggested that up to another 50,000 North Korean soldiers could eventually be deployed, something that Kim Jong Un's sister Kim Yo Jong dismissed as " completely groundless ."

But how is this growing closeness between Russia and North Korea being perceived by China? Over the past 18 months Russia and North Korea have had 23 high level visits involving their ministers, compared to only eight between China and North Korea.

Beijing grows wary of the Russian-North Korean alliance

China's main worry is that deeper ties between Russia and North Korea could increase regional instability and damage China's global reputation. Chinese leader Xi Jinping is also concerned that growing ties between Putin and Kim Jong Un will reduce Xi's leverage over Pyongyang. Official and academic Chinese sources have stressed that Beijing has little interest in a deep trilateral military alignment involving China, North Korea and Russia. While China recognizes that broader Russia-North Korea cooperation increases pressure on the US and other Western allies, it remains uninterested in endorsing a formalized trilateral alignment that would constrain Beijing's strategic goals.

In reality, Russia's relationship with North Korea is entirely transactional. North Korea has happily come through when Russia needed it, but the relationship is not exactly mutual. In 2014, North Korea was among the few countries to recognize Russia's annexation of Crimea, hoping that it would receive economic benefits from Russia in return. This never materialized, however. Bilateral trade between North Korea and Russia remained very limited, only $42 million in 2020, with North Korea ranked as Russia 139 th biggest trading partner.

Today North Korea earns between $7.7 billion and $14.4 billion from the sale of munitions and the deployment of North Korean troops in Russia. North Korea has also benefited from Russia's transfer of sensitive technologies such as naval reactors for nuclear-powered submarines, air defence systems and drone technology. Additionally, with Russia's help North Korea could gain access to autonomous AI-enabled and jet powered drones.

China is increasingly concerned that access to these types of weapons will embolden North Korea, creating greater instability in the region. With Russian help, North Korea's nuclear program and space assets are accelerating, emboldening Kim Jon Un.

China is also worried that as North Korea becomes more powerful and assertive due its closer ties with Russia, its provocations and miscalculations could prompt closer security cooperation between the US, South Korea and Japan, and motivate South Korea and Japan to pursue nuclear weapons. China also does not want a regional conflict to develop which could lead to a refugee crisis, north of the Yalu River that divides North Korea and China.

China's difficult relationship with North Korea

The historical relationship between China and North Korea has been fraught with competition, tension, derision and a profound sense of mistrust rather than mutual respect. Beijing only wants North Korea to be more stable , but not necessarily more powerful. If at best North Korea is seen as a little brother to China, it is regarded as a delinquent one, incapable of doing anything sensible.

This comes at a time when the Chinese public, as expressed through social media posts, is actively hostile towards North Korea, viewing it as an ungrateful troublemaker. Chinese citizens on social media have given Kim unflattering nicknames, including "' Fatty Kim the Third " which the Chinese government had to censor. Chinese web users in an online survey have revealed that many Chinese have felt cold towards North Korea for years.

The Chinese public feels much differently towards Russia. Chinese social media users have shown unquestionable support towards Russia in the war in Ukraine, claiming that " Russia must win ." Putin is portrayed as wise, kind and well-meaning by the Chinese media, while also depicted as an invincible strongman. The Russian people are characterized positively as well, as courageous and admirable. Ultimately, the Chinese see Russia as a strategic ally and an important bulwark against the aggressive West. The same can't be said for North Korea.

While Moscow appears to be cozy with Pyongyang, this is mostly a temporary marriage of convenience with not a lot of love from Russians towards North Korea. Russians are warming to North Korea only slightly, with just one-third of the Russian public seeing North Korea as a close ally in 2026—albeit this is a huge increase from 2021 when it was only 3% according to the independent Levada Centre.

For China, this burgeoning relationship between North Korea and Russia presents more challenges than opportunities. As Moscow deepens its military and strategic ties with Pyongyang, Beijing risks losing some of its leverage over North Korea while facing a more unpredictable neighbor on its doorstep. What may appear to be a useful partnership for Moscow is increasingly uncomfortable for Beijing.

articles.title: Russian drone hits train near Ukraine-Poland border soon after visiting dignitaries passed through
articles.summary: A Russian drone struck a train near the Ukraine- Poland border on Sunday shortly after senior visiting officials — including the former prime ministers of th...
articles.body:
KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — A Russian drone struck a train near the Ukraine- Poland border on Sunday shortly after senior visiting officials — including the former prime ministers of the U.K. and Sweden -- passed through, Ukraine's state rail operator said.

According to Ukrzaliznytsia, a diplomatic train carrying Boris Johnson , Carl Bildt and security advisers from several European Union states had purposely left the station at Yahodyn ahead of schedule. The visitors were on their way back from a security conference in Kyiv.

"It is highly probable that the Russian drone 's intended target was in fact the diplomatic train, which had departed the station earlier than scheduled," the company said in a Telegram post.

Bildt, the former Swedish PM, shared a video on X of the attack at Yahodyn station, near the Yahodyn-Dorohusk border crossing with Poland.

"This wasn't our train, but the one just minutes after us by the Polish border crossing ," Bildt said. "It was evacuated as the Russian drone approached and no one was hurt. Very good safety system. Our train just had an evacuation warning."

Bildt, Johnson and fellow passengers had been in Kyiv for the Yalta European Strategy conference, which is an annual gathering of leaders and experts across politics, business, security and media.

Another train, with former CIA Director David Petraeus on board, was still at Yahodyn station when the drone struck, according to Ukrzaliznytsia.

There were no immediate reports of casualties on any of the trains.

Ukrzaliznytsia said it "constantly adjusts train schedules" to guard against strikes.

"I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning," Johnson wrote in a post on X.

"What we can say for sure is that this is the kind of random and senseless attack Ukrainians are enduring every day — even on civilian railways," he added.

Earlier on Sunday, a Russian drone hit a truck less than a mile from Polish territory, according to border guards, forcing the temporary closure of the Yahodyn-Dorohusk crossing.

articles.title: Russia strikes Ukrainian train near Poland border minutes after Boris Johnson, European leaders pass through
articles.summary: Europe News: A Russian drone struck a passenger train near Ukraine's border with Nato member Poland on Sunday, narrowly missing a train carrying former British Pri.
articles.body: A Russian drone struck a passenger train near Ukraine's border with Nato member Poland on Sunday, narrowly missing a train carrying former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson and other European politicians that had travelled along the same route minutes earlier.The passenger train was hit about 2 kilometres (1.2 miles) from the Polish border, according to Ukraine's railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia. No casualties were reported.The route is frequently used by foreign delegations travelling between Kyiv and Europe. Johnson and other European politicians had been travelling on a diplomatic train along the same line after attending a conference in Kyiv."This wasn’t our train, but the one just minutes after us by the border crossing. It was evacuated as the ‌drone approached and ⁠no one ⁠was hurt," Carl Bildt, former Sweden's Prime Minister said on X.Ukrzaliznytsia said the diplomatic train had departed earlier than scheduled after railway timetables were adjusted in real time because of the continuing threat of Russian strikes."It is entirely possible that the Russian drone's intended target was the diplomatic train, which departed the station earlier ​than scheduled after train timetables were adjusted in real time because of the constant threat of Russian strikes," the railway operator said on Telegram.Johnson, who was also travelling on the train that left the station shortly before the strike, condemned the attack as "random and senseless" in a post on Instagram.The strike took place amid an intensification of long-range attacks by both Russia and Ukraine as fighting along much of the front line remains largely static.Polish foreign minister Radoslaw Sikorski described Russia's increasing attacks near NATO territory as "an escalation."Earlier on Sunday, a truck less than 1 kilometre from Ukraine's border with Poland was also struck. The incident briefly forced the Dorohusk-Yahodyn border crossing to halt operations, according to Polish border guards.Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces had targeted infrastructure used to facilitate military cargo shipments from Europe into western Ukraine.Russia has increasingly targeted Ukrainian border crossings and infrastructure near its Western allies in recent weeks, as both sides intensify attacks on economic and logistical infrastructure more than four years into Moscow's invasion.Russia reports strike near Zaporizhzhia nuclear plantElsewhere, overnight attacks continued across Ukraine and Russia.In the Russian-controlled part of southeastern Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, the head of Russia's state nuclear energy company Rosatom accused Ukraine of striking fuel trucks near the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power station, Europe's largest nuclear plant.The Zaporizhzhia facility has been under Russian control since March 2022 and remains close to the front line. A Ukrainian military spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.In Russia, the mayor of Nizhnekamsk in the Volga River region of Tatarstan said "civilian and industrial" targets in the city had been struck by Ukrainian drones, killing at least two people and injuring several others.Mayor Radmir Belyaev did not specify which targets were hit. Nizhnekamsk is home to a major oil refinery that has previously been targeted.Ukrainian authorities did not immediately comment on the reported strike in Nizhnekamsk but said their forces had struck another refinery in Russia's southern Krasnodar region.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Intolerance and racism’: US senator slams Texas Republican nominee over post targeting Asian students
articles.summary: US News: US Senator John Cornyn has publicly rebuked his fellow Republican Bo French over a social media post targeting students of color celebrating at a Univ.
articles.body: US Senator John Cornyn has publicly rebuked his fellow Republican Bo French over a social media post targeting students of color celebrating at a University of Texas football game, accusing the GOP nominee for Texas railroad commissioner of promoting “intolerance and racism”.The morning after the Texas Longhorns pulled off a major comeback to upset Ohio State, French shared a photo of South Asian students wearing orange and cheering from the stands. French, the former Tarrant County GOP chair, claimed the scene showed “how many Americans have been displaced by foreigners”.“I heard UT graduation this year looked like this. I didn’t believe it. The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined,” French wrote alongside the image.Cornyn urges GOP leaders to speak outCornyn, who lost his Republican primary bid earlier this year, quickly called out French and challenged other Republican officials to condemn the post.“This is the Republican nominee for statewide office,” Cornyn wrote on X. “Are other Republican elected officials going to condemn the intolerance and racism, or look the other way while it becomes normalized. This is how great political parties self-destruct. Sad.”His comments were backed by Democratic state Rep Jon Rosenthal, who is running against French in the November election.“It’s truly unfortunate that so many elected ‘leaders’ will just silently let this pass,” Rosenthal said.Several Texas Republicans also called on French to delete the post. Texas House Speaker Dustin Burrows said political disagreements over immigration policy should not be used to demean people because of their race or ethnicity.“You can oppose immigration policy without demeaning people because of their race or ethnicity — this post has crossed the line,” Burrows said.State Reps Jeff Leach and Lacey Hull also joined calls for French to remove the post.French hits back at CornynFrench, however, doubled down and attacked Cornyn, calling him a “Republican in name only” and accusing him of siding with foreign nationals over Americans.“He and the other America Last losers are mad that Texas Republicans are starting to put America First,” French said in a subsequent post.The controversy comes after a series of clashes between French and Texas Republican leaders over his remarks on immigration and other issues.Several Texas Republican leaders, including Lt Gov Dan Patrick, had previously called for French to step down as Tarrant County Republican chair after he posted a poll asking whether Jews or Muslims posed a bigger threat to America.Patrick had also backed French’s rival in the Republican primary for railroad commissioner, but his position reportedly changed after French won the runoff.Cornyn has become increasingly critical of his own party since losing the Republican primary to Ken Paxton in May. He has also criticised Paxton and said he does not plan to campaign for him in the general election.The senator has also challenged President Donald Trump on several issues, including Trump’s proposal for $5,000 payments to US adults, saying the president would need congressional approval to send out the money.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2023, Reed Hastings invested $100 million to become majority owner of Utah's Powder Mountain; he is now spending another $200 million as the resort expands public and private skiing
articles.summary: US News: What happens when a Netflix co-founder turns his attention from streaming to skiing? For Reed Hastings, it has meant taking control of one of Utah's l.
articles.body: What happens when a Netflix co-founder turns his attention from streaming to skiing? For Reed Hastings, it has meant taking control of one of Utah's largest ski areas and attempting to reshape how a mountain resort operates. Hastings became the controlling owner of Powder Mountain in 2023 after investing $100 million, and his plans have since gone well beyond a conventional ski-resort upgrade. The project combines public skiing with an exclusive private community, new lifts, luxury amenities and a major residential expansion, with major new investments now expanding both its public and private skiing operations.According to Mansion Global, Hastings paid $100 million in 2023 to acquire a controlling share of the Powder Mountain project from its previous owners, Summit Series. The development's first residential phase sold all 39 lots, and the second phase is now adding 34 larger homesites in a new neighbourhood called Prado, along with eight pre-built chalets.Why Hastings bought Powder MountainHastings' connection to Powder Mountain predates his ownership of the resort. He and his wife had already purchased a home there after looking for an alternative to the crowds at Park City. In a 2026 interview reported by POWDER, Hastings said the mountain's quieter atmosphere and fresh snow were major attractions. After spending about 25 years building Netflix, Hastings described Powder Mountain as an opportunity to work on something he cared about outside the technology and entertainment industries. He said he wanted to do something impactful and different from Netflix.The timing was also significant for Powder Mountain itself. Before Hastings took control, the resort had been struggling financially and had not been making money. Hastings' strategy has been to use real estate and private skiing to generate revenue that could help fund improvements to the wider mountain.A ski resort with public and private terrainThe most distinctive part of the plan is the decision to divide access between public skiers and homeowners. Powder Haven, the private residential community, gives homeowners access to private lifts and terrain. At the same time, the majority of Powder Mountain remains available to the general public. Hastings has argued that combining the two sides allows the private development to help finance infrastructure while preserving public skiing.The approach has not been without controversy. Reserving some terrain for homeowners represents a significant departure from the traditional public ski-resort model, and the idea of private skiing has drawn criticism from some members of the skiing community. Hastings, however, has compared the concept to private golf clubs operating alongside the much larger public golf sector.Another $200 million for the mountainHastings has already invested heavily in infrastructure, and his plans call for another $200 million in spending, with much of that investment focused on the Powder Haven side of the project. The wider programme includes new lifts, upgraded infrastructure, improved homeowner services and a large private lodge with high-end amenities.On the public side, Powder Mountain has also been receiving significant upgrades. A $40 million programme announced in 2026 includes three lifts, all intended for public access. One of the biggest additions is the new Don’t Mention It, or DMI, chairlift, which is scheduled to open more than 1,000 acres of advanced terrain to public skiers during the 2026–27 season.An upgraded Sundown lift and a new beginner-focused Doodle lift are also part of the public-side improvements. The resort is additionally planning a 15,000-square-foot Sundown base lodge with ski school facilities, rentals, food and beverage services and skier safety facilities.Powder Haven enters its second phaseThe private residential development is expanding alongside the public ski infrastructure. After all 39 lots in the first Powder Haven neighbourhood, Shelter Hill, sold out, the second phase is bringing 34 larger lots to Prado. Mansion Global reported that the Prado parcels range from one to 4.5 acres and start at about $4 million. Powder Haven is also offering eight pre-built chalets in Shelter Hill, with homes available in configurations of 3,600 or 5,400 square feet. articles.title: Former CIA official David Rush, found with 303 gold bars worth over $40 million, reaches plea agreement in principle as prosecutors cite classified-material litigation
articles.summary: US News: Federal prosecutors and attorneys for former Central Intelligence Agency official David Rush have reached a plea agreement in principle, stopping proc.
articles.body: Federal prosecutors and attorneys for former Central Intelligence Agency official David Rush have reached a plea agreement in principle, stopping proceedings before a grand jury indictment in a case involving $40 million in stolen gold bars and classified operations. A joint court filing submitted to the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia asked for a three-week extension until 8 October to complete the paperwork and an agreed statement of facts. As reported by CBS News and NBC News, both sides said resolving the case before an indictment is in the public interest and would avoid long and costly legal proceedings involving classified national security information. Rush, a former senior executive in the CIA's Directorate of Science and Technology, was arrested in May 2026 after an internal agency inquiry led to a criminal investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.Gold bars and luxury watches foundFederal agents searching Rush's Virginia home found a large collection of government assets hidden in his basement. According to an affidavit filed by FBI Special Agent Matthew T. Johnson, investigators seized 303 individual one-kilogram gold bars, about $2 million in foreign currency and 35 luxury watches, including several Rolex models. The FBI affidavit said that between late 2025 and early 2026, Rush used his senior position to create a fake classified programme. He claimed the programme needed money for confidential operational expenses and requested and received large amounts of gold and foreign currency. Intelligence officials later told investigators that the agency could not find any legitimate operational reason for the funds that had been requested. During an initial detention hearing in June, U.S. Magistrate Judge William Fitzpatrick ordered Rush to remain in custody without bail. The judge considered him a serious flight risk because of his large financial resources, specialised operational experience and ability to avoid detection by law enforcement.False credentials and timecard fraudThe first criminal charges against Rush involved one count of stealing public money through $77,000 in fraudulent military leave payments. Court documents filed in the Eastern District of Virginia said Rush claimed 744 hours of military leave that he had not earned on official timesheets after his honourable discharge from the United States Navy Reserve in 2015. The FBI investigation also found that Rush spent about 17 years at the CIA after repeatedly giving false information about his education and military background on employment and security clearance applications. Background checks could not confirm his claims that he had degrees from Clemson University and the Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute. Investigators also found that Rush had never been a Navy pilot, never attended the U.S. Naval Test Pilot School and never served as a thesis adviser at the Air Force Institute of Technology. He had listed all of these credentials while seeking senior management positions and Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information security clearances.CIA fallout and challenges over classified evidenceRush's arrest led to wider administrative consequences inside the CIA. An internal review launched by CIA Director John Ratcliffe resulted in several senior agency officials being placed on administrative leave. The action followed concerns about management failures in approving Rush's multi-million-dollar requests without proper checks. In their joint request to extend the indictment deadline, Assistant United States Attorney Raizza Ty and defence attorney Jessica Carmichael said taking the case to a public trial would create major legal and procedural challenges under federal laws governing classified information. The court filing said a plea agreement before indictment would remove the need for complicated pre-trial proceedings involving sensitive intelligence sources, methods and classified programmes. District Judge Leonie Brinkema had earlier set a September deadline for an indictment. The joint motion now gives both sides until 8 October to complete the plea terms and submit the final agreement to the court. Rush remains in federal custody while the final plea paperwork is prepared.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station
articles.summary: The former UK PM said "I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning".
articles.body:
A Russian drone has hit a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through.

No casualties were reported after the strike at Yahodyn, which hit the train's engine. All the passengers had been evacuated, Ukrainian authorities said.

Johnson and other European national security advisers, including the UK's Jonathan Powell, had passed along the same line on a different train on their way back from a conference in Kyiv.

Russia said it had struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine, but Ukraine's state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia said that "quite possibly, the target of this drone could have been the diplomatic train".

In a statement, it said the train "had left the station earlier than expected because of the timetable change... due to constant threats of Russian strikes".

It also said an evacuation order for passengers on the hit train had been given "just 15 minutes" before the strike by a Russian jet-propelled drone.

The railway authority also said former CIA chief David Petraeus had been on board another train at Yahodyn station at the time of the drone strike.

Both Ukrainian and Polish authorities said the Russian drone had struck 2km from the Polish border.

Former Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt, who had also attended the conference in Kyiv, told the BBC passengers on board his train had been told to prepare for evacuation before subsequently being allowed to continue their journey.

"On the train I was on we received order to prepare evacuation after it had stopped. But after a number of minutes we were informed that it was clear and we could proceed," he said.

That train then safely arrived at Poland's border station in Dorohusk.

Some reports have suggested Bildt was on the same train as Johnson, but the former UK prime minister has not confirmed any details.

Johnson wrote on X: "I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning.

He said this was "the kind of random and senseless attack Ukrainians are enduring every day - even on civilian railways" and urged Kyiv's allies to urgently provide Ukrainians "the air defences they need".

Ukraine has made repeated pleas to its allies - particularly the US - to provide more interceptors to defend against daily Russian attacks that increasingly use fast-moving ballistic missiles and jet-propelled drones.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the "barbaric strikes" at the Ukraine-Poland border in Yahodyn amounted to "[Russian President Vladimir] Putin's terror 'knocking' directly on the doors of the EU and Nato" and renewed calls for more sanctions on Moscow.

"Putin needs to understand that his barbarism will be met with decisive action that increases the cost of war for him to an unacceptable level. This is the only way to stop him," he said.

In Poland, Prime Minister Donald Tusk held an emergency meeting to discuss the latest developments.

"The escalation of the actions from the Russian side is becoming a reality, and they are getting closer and closer to our border."

Johnson and other top European security advisers were on their way back from the Yalta European Strategy (YES) conference in Kyiv - an annual event that brings together leaders and experts from politics, business, security and mass media.

Russia appears to be escalating its war against Ukraine by targeting trains, railway depots, petrol stations and border crossings.

Earlier this week, two people were killed when Russian drones hit a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

Also this week, a female conductor died in a Russian drone attack on a passenger train in southern Ukraine. Six Ukrzaliznytsia employees were killed after a depot was struck n Kyiv at the start of the month.

In January, Zelensky condemned as "terrorism" a Russian strike on a crowded passenger train in the north-eastern Kharkiv region that left five people dead.

The Russian attacks have significantly damaged Ukraine's vast train network - the main mode of transportation for millions of Ukrainians as all air travel has been suspended since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

European countries are also blaming Russia for suspicious incidents on their territory.

Last week, Germany said Russia was responsible for August's drone attack at Leipzig's airport - a claim denied by Moscow as "absurd".

There have also been a number of suspicious fires at defence facilities from Italy to Estonia, with some of the affected countries blaming Russia.

articles.title: Poland alarmed after Russia attacks train from Kiev to Warsaw
articles.summary: The Russian military on Sunday attacked a passenger train in Ukraine's border region with Poland using a combat drone, with Ukraine's rail company later spec...
articles.body:
Russian military attacked a passenger train in Ukraine's border region with Poland, with speculation that Western diplomats and former politicians onboard might have been the target.

Ukrainian railway company reported that a diplomats' train carrying security advisers from several EU countries and former senior European politicians, including ex-UK prime minister Boris Johnson, was nearby at the time of the attack.

Moscow confirmed attacks on rail infrastructure in western Ukraine, leading to temporary suspension of operations at two border crossings on the Polish side, with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warning of further disruption at the border due to expected intense Russian action in the coming weeks and months.

The Russian military on Sunday attacked a passenger train in Ukraine's border region with Poland using a combat drone, with Ukraine's rail company later speculating that Western diplomats and former politicians onboard, including ex-UK prime minister Boris Johnson, might have been the target.

"The escalation from the Russian side has now become a reality and the examples of it are coming ever closer to our border," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said at a meeting of the crisis team following the incident.

"Putin escalates," Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski wrote on X.

On Sunday, the locomotive of the regular passenger train from Kiev to Warsaw was attacked at the border station of Yahodyn, according to Ukrainian Railways. Passengers were evacuated in time and nobody was harmed, it said. Western politicians travelling to Kiev also rely on the rail link from Poland to Ukraine as the country's airspace is closed.

Ukrainian railway company: diplomats' train nearby

The Ukrainian railway company said in the evening that shortly before the attack a diplomats' train had stopped at Yahodyn station carrying, among others, security advisers from several EU countries and former senior European politicians, including Johnson, who was the UK prime minister in February 2022 when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The group had attended a conference in Kiev the day before.

Another train standing at the station at the time of the attack reportedly carried former CIA chief David Petraeus.

"It is entirely conceivable that the target of this Russian drone could also have been the diplomats' train which, as part of real-time timetable adjustments due to the constant threat of Russian attacks, departed from the station earlier than originally planned," the railway company wrote on Telegram. Timetables were constantly being adjusted because of the war, it said.

Johnson said the Russian attack is yet another example of how Russia is conducting itself in this war.

"I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning," Johnson wrote on X. "What we can say for sure is that this is the kind of random and senseless attack Ukrainians are enduring every day." He did not comment on reports that he had been on another train near the attack.

The Defence Ministry in Moscow confirmed attacks on rail infrastructure in western Ukraine that facilitated transport of military goods from European countries, it said.

Due to the threat of airstrikes, two border crossings on the Polish side temporarily suspended operations. Several hundred people were evacuated for a short time. By the afternoon, the situation at the border had normalized again.

Tusk warns of further disruption at the border

Tusk pointed out that Russia had previously attempted to paralyse border crossings in Moldova. Allies had given indications beforehand that the Russian plan would include attempts to disorganize and possibly destroy Ukrainian border crossings and this could also affect Poland. More intense Russian action was to be expected in the coming weeks and months, Tusk said.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote earlier that Moscow's attacks near the Polish-Ukrainian border in the Volyn region set a locomotive on fire and damaged a petrol station.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called for tougher consequences for Moscow. Russian attacks on the Polish-Ukrainian border were not simply a continuation of attacks on Ukraine's state borders, he wrote on X.

"This is Putin's terror "knocking" directly on the doors of the EU and NATO. Russian barbarians are at your gate, dear partners," he said.

Johnson criticized Western powers for what he sees is a lack of support for Ukraine

"When are we going to give them the air defences they need? Why won't we unfreeze Putin's cash and give it to Ukraine? There is more than 140 billion euro ($163 billion) in a Belgian bank account - and about £10 billion ($13.5 billion) in London. Britain could show a lead," the former British prime minister asserted.

Ukraine has been defending itself against a Russian invasion for more than four and a half years with Western help. Russian attacks repeatedly cause deaths and damage to rail traffic and at stations.

articles.title: In 1984–85, scientists moved 100 rare frogs into restored forest on New Zealand’s Maud Island; nearly 20 years later, 70 founders had been recaptured, and the frogs were heavier and breeding
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover how the translocation of Maud Island frogs in 1984 resulted in a successful breeding population, contributing to endangered species conservation in New Zealand.
articles.body: In 1984, conservationists in New Zealand's Marlborough Sounds moved a population of Maud Island frogs that was confined to a small 15- to 16-hectare area of native forest. The hundred frogs were moved in two consignments to the newly restored habitat in a different location on Maud Island, creating a second population to lessen the species' reliance on one forest fragment. A taxonomic note is also worth mentioning, which is that the species was originally described as Leiopelma pakeka, the scientific name in the first publication on the translocation of the species. The Department of Conservation in New Zealand now usually treats it as a population of Hamilton's frog (Leiopelma hamiltoni).The 1984-85 translocation from Home Bush to Boat BayFrogs were moved in batches: 43 frogs in May 1984 and 57 frogs in May 1985 from the forest patch called Home Bush to the rehabilitated site in Boat Bay, which is half a kilometer distant from the original site. The study was published in the New Zealand Journal of Zoology by Ben D. Bell, Shirley Pledger, and Penelope L. Dewhurst. The researchers have also pointed out that frogs released in 1984 tended to settle nearer to their release site compared to frogs released in 1985, as the latter seemed to avoid the former.Nearly two decades of mark-recapture monitoringSeveral mark–recapture surveys were conducted over a period of almost two decades following the 1984-85 translocation, which allowed the scientists to determine the longevity, dispersal and recruitment of frogs. Seventy of the 100 translocated frogs, as well as 35 recruits born into the population, were recaptured by August 2002. Most of the frogs remained near their release location, while a few moved away from it.Body condition and a high post-settlement survival rateHowever, the translocated individuals went further than just surviving. As the above study indicates, frogs in the Boat Bay area were relatively heavier compared to the frogs in the control group. The researchers attribute this finding, with caution, to low density and high food availability per individual frog. The population initially declined as some founders died, but it later stabilized as recruitment from the local population offset those losses. High survival was recorded following the first period of settlement, but there is no adequate information available from the accessible sources to independently confirm the commonly quoted figures of a 97% survival rate and 33 years life expectancy.A longer view: Two decades of population dataThat longevity is reflected in Bell’s later work. In his 2010 review, The threatened leiopelmatid frogs of New Zealand: Natural history integrates with conservation, published in Herpetological Conservation and Biology, Bell discussed more than two decades of demographic monitoring on Maud Island. He described the long-term work as an unusually extensive study of a wild frog population.According to the Department of Conservation, Hamilton's frog can live for up to 45 years, making it one of the longest-living frogs in the wild. Besides, they have the smallest habitat, moving their centre by just 1.3 metres over a period of 10 years. The study also included cumulative recruitment data after the 1984-85 translocation.Why the translocation still mattersThe Boat Bay project provided lessons for future conservation efforts. In 1997, 300 frogs from the Maud Island population were moved to Motuara Island; according to the Department of Conservation, this was the first time a native New Zealand frog was ever translocated between islands. However, its status depends on biosecurity measures, as the agency has also reported at least one case of mice entering Maud Island in the years since the project. The frogs survived, produced offspring and established a population after being moved to suitable habitat. Few, if any, other New Zealand amphibian conservation projects have been monitored for as long, and the Boat Bay population has become an important case study in New Zealand amphibian conservation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
